objective:
Deploy one contract on Robinhood Chain: ImdGuard, a Uniswap v4 hook for the existing token 0x5f7bb59365ce557c26dbcaa4ee9d39a4b95b7127 (IMD), paired with ETH. No new token and no pool created by the launch; the creator will initialize the pool with this hook afterwards on the PoolManager passed as a constructor argument (0x8366a39CC670B4001A1121B8F6A443A643e40951).
The hook does exactly the following, and nothing else:
1. Take 1.0% of the ETH side of every buy and sell as a hook fee, settled in ETH inside the swap that paid it (mint a claim when the PoolManager cannot pay it directly), and send it to my wallet. Expose claimFees() that anyone may call to redeem claims to the recipient.
2. The owner may pause and unpause swaps. Liquidity can always be removed while paused. Expose pause() and unpause() for the owner and paused() as a view.
3. Protect swappers from sandwich attacks: within one block, swaps against the direction of the block’s first swap execute at no better than the block’s opening price (the AntiSandwichHook pattern).
Owner 0x5Bff2a2FEcD1d6152676813b21346238733bEAB1 may only: pause and unpause swaps, through the functions named above. No other admin function, no backend signer, no upgrade path.
Fees are always taken from the ETH (pair currency) side, never from IMD; a fee the PoolManager cannot pay directly is minted as a claim the recipient can redeem.
Take the PoolManager as a constructor argument and enable only the callbacks the behavior above needs. The deployed address must carry the correct hook permission bits (mine a CREATE2 salt). Owner, if any, is $owner.
Keep the function names exactly as written so the storefront can show them. Composed with The Hooks Store block builder.
